task.title: Open a family tree file
task.shortdesc: Bring a tree from another program, or a copy from a relative, into uFTi.

context.p: A family tree file ends in .ged or .gdz. Put the file in a folder on your Mac first, such as Documents. works on its own copy, so the file you choose stays as it was. says more.

stepresult.p: The Mac's own window for choosing a file opens.

step.cmd: Find the file, choose it, then choose .

stepresult.p: If wrote the file, a box names the tree and counts the people, families, events, sources and notes in it. It says uFTi keeps its own copy; the file you chose is left as it was.
If another program made the file, a page opens first. It says the file was not made by , and asks what the app may do with it.

step.cmd: For a file that another program made, choose or .

choices.choice: keeps a copy of its own in GEDCOM 7, and saves your changes there. The file you chose is not touched. A box then counts what the tree holds.
opens the tree to look at. Nothing is saved, and the file is not touched. To change the tree later, choose on its card to make a copy you can edit.

stepresult.p: The tree opens on , and it has a new card on .

result.p: The cards sit side by side, as many to a row as fit in the window. Choose on a card to make that tree the open one. Choose on a card to see which file it is.
result.note: A card takes its name from the file. If two cards have the same name, choose on each to tell them apart.
